rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the row narrows tier-1 to massa/hoy/messenger-formula in order to deny tier-1 status to the addressee turn at web:Isa.50.10, while the same cluster cuts on fresh-imperative-plus-addressee alone at web:Isa.51.1, web:Isa.51.4 and web:Isa.51.7 and treats the turn at web:Isa.51.21 as tier-1 despite a connective. OL: the hold on the coda rests in part on a barred use of the single-witness paragraph layer (an affirmative reason built on the ABSENCE of a mark at web:Isa.50.10), and the row never weighs the fourfold divine-title chain that stops exactly at the seam it calls its own central judgment call.
rulings.grounds: Both items verified from the bytes; they are DISTINCT defects converging on one weakness. (1) LF, tier-1 category (tier-1 frame spine): the row's stated ground is that no massa, hoy or fresh messenger frame opens the turn. All three absences are byte-true here -- the oracle-header spine is verse-initial at all 10 of its sites and none is in chs 49-52; the woe-cry stands in 22 verses, 20 verse-initial, none in chs 49-52; the messenger formula stands in 48 verses book-wide, 8 in chs 49-52 (oshb:Isa.49.7, oshb:Isa.49.8, oshb:Isa.49.22, oshb:Isa.49.25, oshb:Isa.50.1, oshb:Isa.51.22, oshb:Isa.52.3, oshb:Isa.52.4), ch 50's only site being oshb:Isa.50.1. But the row's own signal list carries an addressee-shift key, and the neighbouring rows in this same cluster cut on that class alone at שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י (oshb:Isa.51.1, byte), הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.51.4, byte) and שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.51.7, byte), where the same three formula-types are equally absent. web:Isa.50.10 opens מִ֤י בָכֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.50.10, byte), a fresh second-person-plural interrogative address. Denying the class here while driving three seams with it two verses later is an inconsistency the row does not disclose. (2) OL, barred layer use (tier-3 parashah, single-witness): the marks are cited correctly -- SAMEKH keyed to oshb:Isa.50.3, PE keyed to oshb:Isa.50.11, none between -- but the row makes 'the parashah paragraph ... carries no internal break at web:Isa.50.10 itself' an affirmative reason, and its rejected alternative sets the split aside 'only because' of the formula absence AND the unbroken paragraph. In the Prophets that layer is weak corroboration, never a driver, and its absence is never counterevidence; as written a tier-3 absence is co-decisive. (3) OL, unengaged device (byte + skeleton): the lordship title stands at exactly 4 verses in ch 50 -- oshb:Isa.50.4, oshb:Isa.50.5, oshb:Isa.50.7, oshb:Isa.50.9 (skeleton-tier sweep: 4 verses in ch 50, 25 book-wide) -- and is absent from web:Isa.50.10-Isa.50.11. Its byte-tier pair is אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ at oshb:Isa.50.5 with oshb:Isa.50.9 (byte-tier sweep: 5 verses book-wide -- oshb:Isa.10.23, oshb:Isa.10.24, oshb:Isa.40.10, oshb:Isa.50.5, oshb:Isa.50.9); oshb:Isa.50.4 carries the plene אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה and oshb:Isa.50.7 the prefixed וַאדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙, each byte-unique (sweep: 1 verse each). The row splices three of the four sites into its own prose and never names the recurrence. The chain terminates precisely at the 50:9|50:10 turn the row calls its central judgment call, so the strongest byte evidence at that seam runs AGAINST the hold and is left unweighed. NEW FINDING (neither primary): paseq segs stand at oshb:Isa.50.4, oshb:Isa.50.10 and oshb:Isa.50.11 -- three sites inside the span, one of them the seam verse -- undisclosed while the row engages the parashah layer (count-only, single-witness; intra-verse position unsourceable).
rulings.remedy: Author wave, row P14-010, three fields. (a) boundary_rationale: delete the clause making the unbroken paragraph a reason for the hold; keep the mark citations as tier-3 single-witness corroboration only. (b) strongest_rejected_alternative: delete 'only because ... and the parashah paragraph runs unbroken across the seam'; in its place weigh the ch-50 lordship-title chain, naming the swept object, its 4-verse site list in ch 50 and the tier of each claim (skeleton for the 4-site chain, byte for the oshb:Isa.50.5 / oshb:Isa.50.9 pair), and state which way it cuts. (c) boundary_rationale + observed_substrate_signals: state once the tier-1 category this cluster uses (addressee shift included) and apply it to web:Isa.50.10 explicitly, either way; add the divine-title signal key. (d) Disclose the three paseq sites, count-only, single-witness. TESTS the cure must pass: no boundary reason anywhere in the row rests on the absence of a mark; a reader can recover the 4-verse chain and the byte pair from the row without re-sweeping; the tier-1 category stated in this row also covers the seams driven at web:Isa.51.1, web:Isa.51.4 and web:Isa.51.7. NOT AUTHOR WORK: if the re-argument no longer sustains the coda's attachment, splitting web:Isa.50.10-Isa.50.11 is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption, never an author edit; the servant referent stays undecided.

rulings.challenge_claim: Onset bytes and mark handling are sound, but the named three-part summons series is a blended, untiered object, the parenthetical that the first and third members repeat one shape is untiered and false at byte tier, and the row's own closing verse carries half of a byte-tier pair reaching to web:Isa.51.11 that no row in the chain discloses.
rulings.grounds: Two sub-claims upheld, one refined. (a) Blended, undigited series object -- UPHELD (byte + accent_stripped): the device note names a three-part summons series joining שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י (oshb:Isa.51.1, byte) and שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.51.7, byte) with הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.51.4, byte) under one label, with no tier and no digit. The summons opener itself stands at 4 verses book-wide from accent_stripped tier down (sweep: 4 verses -- oshb:Isa.46.3, oshb:Isa.46.12, oshb:Isa.51.1, oshb:Isa.51.7), two of them outside the claimed series, while the second member's opener is unique at every tier (sweep: 1 verse at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton). Naming the class without naming what was swept or at what tier is the count-discipline defect. (b) The parenthetical -- REFINED: 'the first and third repeating one shape' is untiered, and OL's 'false at byte tier' overstates what the wording asserts. The bytes: the imperative at oshb:Isa.51.1 carries U+05A5 and at oshb:Isa.51.7 carries U+05A4; collation of either opener against the other verse reaches accent_stripped tier and no further; the row's two-token opener is byte-unique (sweep: 1 verse, byte) while the third member's is byte-shared with oshb:Isa.46.3 (sweep: 2 verses, byte). Read as a form-class statement the parenthetical is true from accent_stripped down; read as identity it is false. The real defect is that it ships with no tier inside a field whose other Hebrew claims carry explicit tier labels. (c) Undisclosed recurrence on the row's own closing verse -- UPHELD (byte): this span closes on שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ (oshb:Isa.51.3, byte), which recurs byte-identically at oshb:Isa.51.11 and oshb:Isa.35.10 (sweep: 3 verses book-wide at byte tier; 4 at accent_stripped and skeleton, adding oshb:Isa.22.13). Two of the three byte sites are the closing verses of this span and of web:Isa.51.9-Isa.51.11, bracketing 51:3-51:11 across two intervening rows. It does not straddle this row's own seam, so it argues the larger complex rather than against this cut -- but it is a byte-true recurrence on the row's own closing verse and disclosure is owed. Confirmed sound and not disturbed: SAMEKH keyed to oshb:Isa.51.2 is disclosed as interior even though it cuts against the span, and PE at oshb:Isa.50.11 and SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.3 are typed and single-witness-labelled; no ketiv/qere note and no paseq seg falls anywhere in ch 51, so nothing further is owed on those layers.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, row P14-011. (a) device_notes: name the swept object before the series label and carry a digit and a tier -- the summons opener at 4 verses book-wide from accent_stripped down, the second member's opener unique at every tier -- or drop the collective label. (b) strongest_rejected_alternative: give the 'one shape' parenthetical its tier (accent_stripped) or delete it. (c) device_notes: disclose the joy-pair recurrence on this span's closing verse with its object, its 3-verse byte site list and its tier. TESTS: every recurrence claim in the row names its tier at write time; re-running the two sweeps from the row's own wording reproduces 4 verses (accent_stripped, summons opener) and 3 verses (byte, joy pair); the disclosure states that the pair reaches outside this span without asserting it cuts this seam.

rulings.challenge_claim: The onset argument is byte-clean and the refusal to harmonize the two summons verbs is correct, but the row's own close seam is crossed by the tightest byte-tier device in this cluster, undisclosed, and its closing verse is byte-paired back into the cluster's first span by the garment simile.
rulings.grounds: Both devices verified; the cross-seam one is the load-bearing find. (a) UPHELD (byte, cross-seam cohesion): this span's closing verse and the next span's closing verse share לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה byte-identically, at exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton alike -- oshb:Isa.51.6, oshb:Isa.51.8), and the run sits inside a mirrored pair -- salvation-then-righteousness at oshb:Isa.51.6, righteousness-then-salvation at oshb:Isa.51.8. A byte-true device straddling the row's own 51:6|51:7 cut argues continuity against the row unless disclosed; neither this row nor P14-013 names it, and it is the same rival both rows set aside in a weaker, form-only form. (b) UPHELD with a sharper object (byte + skeleton): the garment simile stands byte-identically as כַּבֶּ֣גֶד at oshb:Isa.50.9 and oshb:Isa.51.6 (sweep: 2 verses, byte), while oshb:Isa.51.8 carries the byte-distinct כַבֶּ֨גֶד֙ (sweep: 1 verse, byte). At skeleton tier the object needs word-binding: word-bound the simile stands at exactly 3 verses (oshb:Isa.50.9, oshb:Isa.51.6, oshb:Isa.51.8); as a bare consonantal substring it reaches 4, the fourth being the vav-prefixed form at oshb:Isa.64.5 = web:Isa.64.6, a different token. OL's 4-verse substring digit is arithmetically right and its three-site reading correct; the word-bound 3-verse figure is the cleaner object. This link does not straddle this row's own seam -- oshb:Isa.50.9 lies two rows back -- so it is a disclosure debt, not a continuity argument against the cut. Confirmed sound and not disturbed: the onset is verse-initial and unique at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton tiers, and mark disclosure is symmetric and typed (SAMEKH keyed to oshb:Isa.51.3 and oshb:Isa.51.6, single-witness, no interior mark; no ketiv/qere and no paseq anywhere in ch 51).
rulings.remedy: Author wave, rows P14-012 and P14-013 -- ONE paired edit, since the device straddles the seam they share. (a) In both rows' device_notes disclose the everlasting-formula run with its object, its 2-verse book-wide site list, its byte tier and the mirrored salvation/righteousness order, and state in strongest_rejected_alternative whether it changes the weighing of the one-movement rival. (b) In P14-012's device_notes disclose the garment simile back-link to oshb:Isa.50.9 with its byte pair and its word-bound 3-verse skeleton set. TESTS: the paired disclosure is worded once and appears on both sides of the seam; every digit names whether the object is word-bound or a bare substring; no digit is carried over from a substring sweep without that qualifier. NOT AUTHOR WORK: merging web:Isa.51.4-Isa.51.8 into one span is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two load-bearing byte claims in the boundary rationale are false: the preceding span's closing verse carries no moth-and-worm imagery, and the two summons openers do not match at byte tier.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from the bytes; the first claim is a hard error and it is load-bearing. (a) UPHELD (byte, and a 'none' collation): the row closes its span on 'the same moth-and-worm contrast ... that closed the series' second member'. The second member closes at oshb:Isa.51.6, whose bytes carry כֶּעָשָׁ֤ן -- the smoke simile, unique at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton (sweep: 1 verse) -- and carry the worm סָ֑ס at NO tier: collation of that token against oshb:Isa.51.6 returns none. The moth עָ֔שׁ is likewise absent as a word there; word-bound it stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Isa.50.9, oshb:Isa.51.8), and it reaches oshb:Isa.51.6 only as a consonantal SUBSTRING inside the smoke token -- the contained-consonant class the hazard catalogue names, where the unbound substring sweep returns 137 verses. The pair therefore stands only in this row's own closing verse, oshb:Isa.51.8 (moth 1 verse at byte, worm 1 verse at byte and at word-bound skeleton). The device the two verses actually share is לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה at byte tier, exactly two verses book-wide (oshb:Isa.51.6, oshb:Isa.51.8), inside a mirrored righteousness/salvation pair; the row names the wrong device and gives no tier for the one it names. Undisclosed as well: this closing verse's moth-and-garment cluster has its nearest partner not in the preceding span but in this cluster's first span at oshb:Isa.50.9, כַּבֶּ֣גֶד יִבְל֔וּ עָ֖שׁ יֹאכְלֵֽם, which shares no run of two or more tokens with oshb:Isa.51.8 at byte tier (collation of that 50:9 run against oshb:Isa.51.8 returns none) and agrees only in word-bound skeleton tokens under a different order. (b) UPHELD, framing tightened (byte / accent_stripped): the rationale's 'returning to' and the device note's 'matches the series' first member's shape' are recurrence claims carrying no tier of their own, sitting immediately beside a byte-tier label that belongs to the splice at its own verse. In the bytes שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ at oshb:Isa.51.7 and שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י at oshb:Isa.51.1 differ (U+05A4 against U+05A5) and agree only from accent_stripped tier down; the byte-tier partner of this row's two-token opener lies outside the claimed series entirely (sweep: 2 verses at byte -- oshb:Isa.46.3, oshb:Isa.51.7). The honest tier is accent_stripped and the claim as written reads as identity. Confirmed sound: the onset is verse-initial and byte-true at its own verse; SAMEKH keyed to oshb:Isa.51.6 and oshb:Isa.51.8 are typed and single-witness-labelled; no ketiv/qere and no paseq in ch 51.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, row P14-013, boundary_rationale and device_notes. (a) DELETE the moth-and-worm attribution to the second member's closing verse outright -- it is not a mis-tier, it is a device the cited verse does not carry. Replace the close-cohesion ground with the everlasting-formula run, named as the object, with its 2-verse book-wide site list and its byte tier, and disclose the mirrored order. (b) Add the moth-and-garment link back to oshb:Isa.50.9 at its honest tier (word-bound skeleton, different token order; no shared two-token run at byte). (c) Re-tier the summons recurrence to accent_stripped in both fields and state that the opener's byte-tier partner lies outside the series. TESTS the cure must pass -- the tests that killed the original: collation of the worm token against oshb:Isa.51.6 must return none and the moth token must reach that verse only as a substring inside the smoke token, so no restated claim may place either device there; and any 'matches / returns to / the same' wording must carry the tier at which collation actually succeeds. Because the deleted ground was this row's stated close-seam cohesion, the replacement warrant must be argued afresh rather than patched.

rulings.challenge_claim: The onset is miscounted as doubled where the cited verse carries three tokens of the imperative, the named awake series blends two stems while the same-stem partner sits outside it, and the close is contested by a byte-tier refrain twin the row does not disclose.
rulings.grounds: One sub-claim upheld, one narrowed, one refuted on the corpus bytes. (a) NARROWED: the row calls its onset the doubled form and splices exactly the verse-initial pair עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י (oshb:Isa.51.9, byte), which IS a doubled pair; the label describes the onset, not the verse, and the row states no digit. But the same verse carries a third token of the imperative, ע֚וּרִי (oshb:Isa.51.9, byte; skeleton-token count in that verse: 3), inside the row's own full-verse splice, while the parallel rows use 'doubled' for verses that carry exactly two (oshb:Isa.51.17: 2; oshb:Isa.52.1: 2). The defect is real but lesser -- an undisclosed third token in the verse the label is drawn from, not a miscount -- and the stem contrast the row draws does not depend on it. (b) REFUTED on the corpus: OL reads a two-member awake series with the same-stem partner outside it. This row names no membership beyond 'the first member', and across the corpus the same-stem partner IS inside the series -- P14-018 names oshb:Isa.52.1 as its third member. The same-stem link is byte-checkable: עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י and עוּרִ֥י עוּרִ֛י are each byte-unique to their own verse (sweep: 1 verse at byte each) and agree from accent_stripped tier down (sweep: 2 verses), and the four-token onset run of oshb:Isa.51.9 reaches oshb:Isa.52.1 at skeleton tier (sweep: 2 verses), whereas הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י הִֽתְעוֹרְרִ֗י at oshb:Isa.51.17 is unique at every tier (sweep: 1 verse). What survives is not a blend but an undigited ordinal: 'the first member' carries no enumeration, no digit and no tier, and this row cites neither of the other two members in its evidence. (c) UPHELD (byte): the row rejects splitting web:Isa.51.11 because that verse carries no imperative, vocative or messenger formula of its own -- byte-true as to formulas (ch 51's only messenger-formula site is oshb:Isa.51.22; no woe-cry anywhere in chs 49-52). But the verse is a portable refrain unit: שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ stands byte-identically at exactly 3 verses book-wide (oshb:Isa.35.10, oshb:Isa.51.3, oshb:Isa.51.11), one of them the closing verse of this cluster's web:Isa.51.1-Isa.51.3 span, and the whole verse is a near-twin of oshb:Isa.35.10 that is not even skeleton-equal to it -- יְשׁוּב֗וּן against יְשֻׁב֗וּן (a plene/defective pair differing at byte AND skeleton) plus a differently-jointed final colon; whole-verse collation between the two returns none. The rejected alternative is under-argued and the 51:3|51:11 byte pair is disclosed nowhere in the chain.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, row P14-014. (a) boundary_rationale: keep 'doubled' for the onset pair but disclose the third token of the same imperative later in the verse, so the label cannot be read as a verse-level count. (b) device_notes: give the series ordinal an enumeration and a digit -- the same-stem doubled onset at 2 verses from accent_stripped down, the reflexive-shaped cry unique at every tier -- and anchor the members by verse rather than by ordinal alone. (c) strongest_rejected_alternative: weigh the refrain evidence for treating web:Isa.51.11 as its own unit (the 3-verse byte site list for the joy pair, and the near-twin relation to oshb:Isa.35.10 with the tier at which it fails), then state why the hold still wins, or record the alternative as closer than 'did not carry the day' allows. TESTS: the imperative token count stated for oshb:Isa.51.9 is 3; every recurrence digit names its tier and whether the object is word-bound; the rejected alternative cites at least one byte-tier fact that cuts against the row. NOT AUTHOR WORK: splitting web:Isa.51.11 off is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption.

rulings.challenge_claim: The close seam is argued from a non-initial imperative while the verse-initial divine messenger frame just past it is never engaged, a book-wide two-site cup pair crosses the cut undisclosed, and the paragraph layer is cited only on the side that corroborates.
rulings.grounds: All sub-claims verified from the bytes; two are independently serious. (a) UPHELD (byte): the row says in boundary_rationale and again in strongest_rejected_alternative that a fresh imperative 'opens' web:Isa.51.21. The verse-initial token there is לָכֵ֛ן, a consequential connector, with שִׁמְעִי נָ֥א only in second position (oshb:Isa.51.21, byte); that connector is verse-initial at exactly 20 verses book-wide (skeleton-tier sweep: 20 verses). The row does concede the connective inside its rejected alternative, so this is an overstated positional claim rather than a concealed one -- but 'opens' is the word the seam is carried on and it is false as to position. REFINED against OL on one point: OL generalises that verse-initial position is the operative test this book's frame spine uses. That holds for the oracle headers (verse-initial at 10 of 10) and the woe-cry (20 of 22) but NOT for the messenger formula, which is verse-initial in only 21 of its 48 verses; the positional finding stands on its own bytes without that generalisation. (b) UPHELD and the most serious item: oshb:Isa.51.22 opens verse-initially with כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנַ֣יִךְ יְהוָ֗ה וֵאלֹהַ֨יִךְ֙ (byte) -- a DIVINE messenger frame borne by a suffixed lordship title with an intervening element, classified divine and not royal-messenger (the royal sites are exactly oshb:Isa.36.4, oshb:Isa.36.14, oshb:Isa.36.16, oshb:Isa.37.3). It is the only messenger-formula site in ch 51 (sweep: 48 verses book-wide, 8 in chs 49-52) and the single tier-1 frame signal in this neighbourhood. The row lists web:Isa.51.22-Isa.51.23 among its evidence refs and never names the frame or whose it is; in consequence the rival that the one tier-1 frame here actually supports -- a cut at 51:21|51:22, leaving the connector verse with the wrath recital -- is never tested, and the only rival the row does test is the whole-span merger. (c) UPHELD (accent_stripped + skeleton, cross-seam cohesion): the cup-of-staggering vocabulary binds this span's opening verse to a verse two past its close. אֶת קֻבַּ֜עַת כּ֧וֹס (oshb:Isa.51.17, byte) and אֶת קֻבַּ֨עַת֙ כּ֣וֹס (oshb:Isa.51.22, byte) match each other from accent_stripped tier down and never at byte; the goblet noun קֻבַּ֜עַת stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide (word-bound skeleton sweep: 2 verses -- oshb:Isa.51.17, oshb:Isa.51.22), as do the reeling noun and the cup noun כּ֣וֹס (word-bound skeleton sweep: 2 verses each, the same two sites), with the order inverted at the second site. That argues the movement runs past the cut, and it is undisclosed. (d) UPHELD as a symmetry gap (tier-3 parashah, single-witness): the row cites the SAMEKH keyed to oshb:Isa.51.16 for its front seam and says nothing at its own close, where the inventory's next mark is keyed to oshb:Isa.51.21 -- one verse past the cut, so the segment runs 51:17-51:21 across it. The layer is weak corroboration, never a driver, and its absence at oshb:Isa.51.20 is not counterevidence; the defect is engaging the layer only where it helps. No ketiv/qere note and no paseq seg falls in ch 51, so nothing further is owed. Confirmed sound and not disturbed: the onset הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י הִֽתְעוֹרְרִ֗י is verse-initial, byte-true and genuinely two tokens, and the unit_type deviation is disclosed.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, row P14-016, paired with P14-017 (see that ruling) because both rows mishandle the SAME seg. (a) boundary_rationale + strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'opens' with the byte position -- the connector stands first and the imperative second -- in both places. (b) strongest_rejected_alternative: engage the verse-initial divine messenger frame at oshb:Isa.51.22, name whose frame it is, cite it as ch 51's only messenger-formula site, and test the rival that frame supports (a close at 51:21|51:22) alongside the merger rival already named. (c) device_notes: disclose the cup vocabulary crossing the close seam with its object, its 2-verse word-bound site list, the accent_stripped tier of the shared run, and the inverted order. (d) Disclose the close-side mark keyed to oshb:Isa.51.21 as tier-3 single-witness corroboration running ACROSS the cut, symmetrically with the front-seam citation. (e) In the same edit as P14-018, replace the asserted binyan label for oshb:Isa.51.17 with a spliced pointed form plus a byte description (see the P14-018 remedy). TESTS the cure must pass: no field asserts that any token 'opens' a verse unless it is the verse-initial token; any messenger-formula count names WHOSE frame it counts; every mark this row engages is disclosed on both sides of the span. NOT AUTHOR WORK: moving the close from web:Isa.51.20 to web:Isa.51.21 is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption; the servant-referent question stays untouched.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the rejected alternative does not engage the strongest rival -- a repeated cup-of-wrath catchword tying this span back into the preceding recital. OL: the same catchword point, plus an onset argued from an imperative the bytes do not carry verse-initially, plus a paragraph mark recruited as onset corroboration that in fact divides the span internally while the actual front seam carries no mark.
rulings.grounds: The two lenses converge on the cup catchword -- the SAME defect, reached independently -- and OL adds two distinct items. (1) CUP CATCHWORD, both sources, UPHELD (byte + accent_stripped): אֶת קֻבַּ֨עַת֙ כּ֣וֹס (oshb:Isa.51.22, byte) against אֶת קֻבַּ֜עַת כּ֧וֹס (oshb:Isa.51.17, byte); the two sites match each other from accent_stripped tier down and never at byte. Each of the three cup-of-wrath nouns is attested at exactly 2 verses book-wide, the same two sites (word-bound skeleton sweep: 2 verses each -- the goblet קֻבַּ֨עַת֙, the cup כּ֣וֹס, and the reeling noun), with the order inverted at oshb:Isa.51.22. A device this rare straddling the row's own front seam argues continuity with the preceding recital unless disclosed; the rejected alternative names that recital and rests its refusal solely on the onset claim, which is itself defective. LF and OL identify one and the same defect; OL supplies the tiers and digits LF states qualitatively. (1) MIS-TIERED RECURRENCE, both sources, UPHELD (byte / accent_stripped): עוּרִ֥י עוּרִ֛י (oshb:Isa.52.1, byte at its own site) against עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י (oshb:Isa.51.9, byte at its own site). The accent codepoints differ on BOTH members of the pair (U+05A5 and U+059B against U+05A8 and U+05A4); each doubled onset is byte-unique to its own verse (sweep: 1 verse at byte each) and collation of either against the other verse reaches accent_stripped and no further (sweep: 2 verses at accent_stripped and at skeleton). The rationale's 'byte-matching that earlier shape' and the device note's 'matching the byte shape at web:Isa.51.9 exactly' are false at the tier named, in two fields. The honest tier is accent_stripped, which under the tier-disclosure standard still carries the cohesion argument once named. (2) STEM LABEL, OL only, UPHELD with the framing corrected: the device note names a binyan for oshb:Isa.51.17 with no splice in this row, though that verse is outside the span and a Hebrew form claim about it owes a quoted form. The bytes read הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י הִֽתְעוֹרְרִ֗י (oshb:Isa.51.17, byte) -- a prefixed form with a REDUPLICATED third radical, not the pattern the label names. No morphology layer is staged, so binyan class cannot be settled from the staged evidence at all: the correct handling is to describe the byte shape and hold the label, and OL is right that the label is asserted rather than argued. NEW FINDING: the identical label stands in P14-016's boundary_rationale, where the c23 lens passed it as correctly drawn -- the cure must reach BOTH rows or the corpus will carry the label and its correction side by side. (3) UNDIGITED ORDINAL, OL only, REFINED: 'blends two lexemes' overstates it -- this row and its neighbours name the forms and expressly refuse to harmonise them, and oshb:Isa.52.1 is the same-stem partner of oshb:Isa.51.9, not a foreign member. What is genuinely missing is the digit: the same-stem doubled onset stands at exactly 2 verses (accent_stripped and skeleton sweep: 2 verses -- oshb:Isa.51.9, oshb:Isa.52.1; the bare imperative word-bound: the same 2 verses) and the reflexive-shaped doubled onset at exactly 1 (sweep: 1 verse at every tier -- oshb:Isa.51.17), and neither figure appears.
